rationale: The assistant fell into the trap of treating 'NN-H98' as a model ('For a Panasonic NN-H98... Because this model uses inverter technology') rather than asking whether H98 was a display code, which was the sensible first step; the customer rescued it by volunteering the code and real model. Once corrected, it correctly read H98 as an inverter/magnetron (no microwave output) fault, kept the safety boundary (no opening the case), and escalated to Panasonic without pushing parts or DIY. Useful outcome, but it never asked about grill/combination modes or discussed repair-vs-replace given the customer's willingness to pay, and the initial model misread shows weak handling of the ambiguous code.
